description: FloodMapping is an R package for making flood-extent maps from U.S. Height Above Nearest Drainage layers and National Water Model flows. It acquires and prepares large source layers, then applies forecast or historical discharge values to map inundation for a selected area. Inputs include HAND elevations, catchment mappings and flow series; outputs are flood-extent rasters suitable for R mapping tools. Its documented coverage is the contiguous United States, while map resolution and period depend on the selected inputs. The package is free under MIT terms. Initial processing is slow because raw geographic inputs have to be collected and formatted; later mapping can reuse the local cache. A threshold or prestage adjustment can change the resulting extent, so mapped areas are scenario estimates, not observed flooding. The README contains a Lawrence, Kansas example. It can support flood-defence and emergency-service planning, but the example was not reproduced and no HAND or flow data was downloaded. The National Water Model (model-noaa-national-water-model) supplies related flow forecasts.
